messages:
Sam (PM): Heads-up: we need a compact GA acceptance checklist focusing on SLA commitments, observability, support routing, and pricing guardrails. I want a one-pager and owners by EOD. Quick volunteers?
Mei (Product Ops): I can collate the checklist and keep it to 1 page. Will need explicit pass/fail criteria per item.
Raj (Infra): I'll take observability/dashboards. Will define the minimum panels and required telemetry retention for GA.
Clara (SRE): I'll do the incident/playbook piece + escalation steps. Also want an error-budget policy to gate rollouts.
Zoe (Docs): I'll do the public SLA page + internal operational runbook skeleton. Need owners to provide thresholds.
Mateo (Sales): I'll review pricing guardrails and default quotas for self-serve customers. Also need a simple explainer for customers about what GA means for availability and support.
Sam (PM): Good. Core GA asks (draft):
- SLA: uptime SLA for Dedicated (99.9%), hosted "operational" guarantee (not full SLA) for GA; formal hosted SLA to follow.
- Latency SLOs: define by model-size/seq-length buckets, only small-short guaranteed at GA.
- Support: 24x5 email/support channel for GA; paid SLA with response times is sales-managed.
- Monitoring: baseline dashboards + alert list; 30d metric retention for GA telemetry.
- Pricing: default soft quota with overage alerts; burst requires opt-in commercial terms.
Mei (Product Ops): Can we make the hosted vs dedicated language concrete? Customers often read GA and expect parity. We should be explicit: hosted has limited guarantees during GA; Dedicated customers with reserved pools get stronger guarantees.
Sam (PM): Yes, doc wording must be explicit. Zoe, call out phrasing like "Hosted customers should expect transient latency variance during GA; contact sales for dedicated SLAs."
Zoe (Docs): Noted. Also propose a one-line "When to contact support" flowchart.
Raj (Infra): Observability minimums (draft):
- Panels: tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency by model, error rate by endpoint, kv-cache hit_rate, queue depth, autoscale events, fallback counts.
- Alerts (examples): `llm.latency.p99 > baseline*1.8 for 5m`, `llm.error_rate > 1% for 1m`, `llm.queue.depth > 500`
- Retention: 30d metrics, 90d aggregated logs.
Clara (SRE): Error budget + rollout gate idea: each service has a weekly error budget (e.g., 0.1% errors). Canary rollouts consume budget; if consumption > 50% in 24h, pause rollout. Add auto-abort for canaries on specific alerts.
Mei (Product Ops): That gives us a measurable gate. Add a checklist item: "simulated surge test completed" before full rollout.
Sam (PM): Agreed. Also require shadow traffic test and smoke tests in each region before opening GA.
Mateo (Sales): On pricing guardrails: default free-tier token quota (e.g., 500k tokens/mo) + 3 quota tiers. For burst: notify at 60% and 85%, require contract at 100% for auto-burst. Also need a chargeback/backstop process if burst leads to unexpectedly high bills.
cost-bot: Alert policy draft saved: budget.notify@60, budget.escalate@85, budget.hold@100.
Zoe (Docs): I'll add a short customer-facing section: "Billing safety nets" and an internal section: "How to apply emergency holds" with steps.
Clara (SRE): Runbook skeleton (quick): incident detection -> triage -> containment -> rollback decision -> remediation -> postmortem. Add who to page: product-support, eng-oncall, infra-sre.
Raj (Infra): One more infra ask: define model-variant fallback behavior in docs and metrics. We should emit `llm.fallback.reason` and count.
Sam (PM): Good catch. Add to checklist: "fallback transparency" — logs + customer notice if we route to cheaper variant for availability.
Mei (Product Ops): Timeline: Mei to own checklist collated by EOD. Raj to PR dashboard list by tomorrow noon. Clara to publish runbook skeleton + escalation matrix by tomorrow EOD. Zoe to draft SLA + customer FAQ by Monday. Mateo to confirm pricing tiers and quota language by Monday.
Sam (PM): Final sign-off meeting Monday 10:00 PT. Drop PR links here. Keep checklist minimal and binary (pass/fail). :white_check_mark:
